variants.headline: Looking back: strike collapses
variants.sub: The union {name} has seen its strike collapse.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The strike by the union {name} had collapsed.

The gazette records the collapse without describing it as a negotiated settlement. The end of an action and the resolution of a dispute are distinct propositions. A reliable public notice should also avoid assigning a cause to the collapse where the particulars of that cause have not been supplied.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. Collapse does not prove every adverse claim about the people involved, and a fair hearing should survive an outcome that lends itself to easy recrimination.

variants.headline: Looking back: labour action loses its course
variants.sub: The strike by {name} has ended in collapse.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: The union {name} had seen its strike collapse.

The gazette records the collapse without describing it as a negotiated settlement. The end of an action and the resolution of a dispute are distinct propositions. A reliable public notice should also avoid assigning a cause to the collapse where the particulars of that cause have not been supplied.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. Collapse does not prove every adverse claim about the people involved, and a fair hearing should survive an outcome that lends itself to easy recrimination.

variants.headline: Looking back: a strike ends in collapse
variants.sub: The strike by the union {name} has collapsed.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: The strike by {name} had ended in collapse.

The gazette records the collapse without describing it as a negotiated settlement. The end of an action and the resolution of a dispute are distinct propositions. A reliable public notice should also avoid assigning a cause to the collapse where the particulars of that cause have not been supplied.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. Collapse does not prove every adverse claim about the people involved, and a fair hearing should survive an outcome that lends itself to easy recrimination.
